task.description:
WF-03 STEP 5 -- CLOSE THE ISSUE for ISS-0440. Every gate has PASSED: SECURITY-REVIEWER (03b), REVIEWER (03c, two non-blocking MINORs filed as ISS-0442/ISS-0443), TEST-DESIGNER (04), TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (04b, independently reproduced mutants M1 and M2 at 40/43 each), TEST-RUNNER (04c: full suite 3156 passed / 0 failures, 43 in the changed file, lint 0 new violations, compile --warnings-as-errors clean).

THE CENTRAL JUDGEMENT OF THIS STEP, and do not treat it as a formality: WHICH TERMINAL STATUS DOES THIS RUN ACTUALLY SUPPORT? Read ISSUE_QUEUE.md's 'Issue status vocabulary' in full BEFORE writing the status line. The tension is real and you must resolve it on the evidence, not by momentum:
  - ISS-0440's stated SCOPE was 'make the violation structurally impossible rather than documenting it a seventh time', and it explicitly forbids closing by adding a seventh tally line to docs/anti-patterns.md.
  - What SHIPPED, per the design after three rework cycles specifically about overclaiming, is Mechanism A (tooling: --dir, restricted --autofix over a closed 3-value map, an unconditional scan banner, an empty-scope guard) plus Mechanism B (a procedural clause in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.3). The design's own settled position -- upheld by REVIEWER at 03c item 3 -- is that Mechanism B is PROCEDURAL and reaches neither Tier 3 nor structural merge-blocking, and that detection is guaranteed only once the linter executes.
  - ISS-0441 (filed this run, MAJOR, still open) documents that main has NO branch protection at all, so CI is advisory and every 'hard' gate in this pipeline is procedurally rather than structurally enforced.
  So: did this run REMOVE the root cause (-> `resolved`, which requires a regression test proving it -- you have one), or did it ship verified, useful work while leaving the root cause in place (-> `instrumented`, which REQUIRES a `superseded_by: ISS-NNNN` pointer naming the successor that carries the remaining work)? Decide this deliberately and JUSTIFY IT IN THE RECORD in a few sentences a later run can audit. Both answers are defensible on the facts; an unjustified one is not. Note if you choose `instrumented` you must have a successor issue to point at -- ISS-0441 already exists and covers the structural-enforcement gap; judge whether it is the right supersedor or whether a narrower successor should be filed first. If you choose `resolved`, state plainly what the fix does NOT cover so the record does not overclaim, since overclaiming is the exact defect this run's design was reworked three times to avoid.

THEN, mechanically:
  1. Write docs/issues/ISS-0440.yaml's terminal status with THAT status's OWN key pair, exactly as ISSUE_QUEUE.md specifies: `resolved` -> resolved_in_run:/resolved_at:; `instrumented` -> resolved_in_run:/resolved_at: PLUS a required superseded_by:. Use a real UTC timestamp from `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`, not memory. Cite the regression test path and the design doc.
  2. GITHUB CLOSE -- github_issue is 849 and this is a HARD requirement, not discretion. `gh issue close 849 --comment "<...>"`. The comment text BRANCHES ON THE STATUS you chose and must claim only what this run did: `resolved` -> 'Fixed in WF03-ISS0440-20260903. See docs/issues/ISS-0440.yaml and the regression test at <path>.'; `instrumented` -> 'Investigated in WF03-ISS0440-20260903; verified work shipped but the root cause is NOT removed. See docs/issues/ISS-0440.yaml and the successor issue <ISS-NNNN>.' A close with no --comment is this step NOT DONE. If gh is unreachable, say so explicitly and quote the error -- do not silently skip it.
  3. ANTI-PATTERNS. docs/anti-patterns.md's existing entry for this defect class records occurrences 1-6 and declares 're-document it' EXHAUSTED. Do NOT add a seventh tally line as the closing action -- that is the forbidden move. DO update the entry to point at what now exists (the --autofix remediation path, the HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.3 clause) and at this run, so a future agent hitting occurrence 8 finds the tooling instead of re-analysing from scratch. Keep it short; the entry already carries the analysis.
  4. Confirm ISS-0442 and ISS-0443 are `open` and correctly cross-referenced from ISS-0440's `related:` so the follow-up work is claimable and not orphaned.

Run `mix letflow.lint_handoffs` before completing and confirm 0 new violations. Complete the handoff with PASS in result.status and route to Step Final (GIT MERGE). Commit to branch feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903.

result.summary:
TERMINAL STATUS CHOSEN: `instrumented`, not `resolved` -- deliberate, not default-to-green. Reasoning: ISS-0440's diagnosis named the actual bar -- 'the check must fire as a mechanical consequence of an action the pipeline cannot avoid taking, with zero agent decision about whether to run it.' What shipped (Mechanism A: --dir/--autofix over a closed {PASS,COMPLETE,DONE}->COMPLETED map, unconditional scan banner, empty-scope guard in lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex; Mechanism B: a procedural clause in docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.3) is real, verified, useful work -- SECURITY-REVIEWER PASS, REVIEWER PASS (two non-blocking MINORs filed as ISS-0442/ISS-0443), full suite 3156 passed/0 failures, changed-file 43 tests independently re-derived three times (TEST-DESIGNER, TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR applying mutants M1/M2 itself at 40/43 each, TEST-RUNNER's own re-run), lint_handoffs itself 0 new violations. But neither mechanism meets the diagnosis's bar: --autofix only runs when an agent invokes the task (same manual trigger as before this run, just cheaper to fix once caught), and Mechanism B is explicit in its own text that it 'is not a code-enforced gate.' REVIEWER (step-03c item 3/4) independently confirmed neither the docs text nor the code overclaims beyond the design's settled position: 'always detected and recorded', explicitly not 'cannot be merged'. ISS-0441 (filed this run, MAJOR, open) further shows even CI is not a structural merge gate (no branch protection on main) -- named explicitly in the design as the reason ISS-0440's own guarantee is worded the way it is. An agent can still write an invalid top-level status today with zero structural obstruction at write time; occurrence 8 remains possible under the letter of the original defect, though it now self-heals cheaply once caught instead of requiring a manual field edit. That gap is exactly what `resolved` would falsely assert closed, so `instrumented` is the honest terminal status.

SUPERSEDED_BY: ISS-0441 -- not a placeholder, already exists (MAJOR, open, filed this same run), scoped to the actual remaining gap (structural/merge-blocking enforcement of pipeline gates generally). Considered and rejected a narrower successor scoped only to 'trigger the linter without agent choice' (e.g. a tracked pre-push hook per the original diagnosis's option (a)): rejected because a client-side hook is bypassable and would not close the structural hole ISS-0441 documents at the merge/server level, whereas fixing ISS-0441 (making CI, which already runs the linter, an actual merge gate) would make this defect class's write-time gap moot as a side effect.

WHAT DOES NOT COVER (stated so the record does not overclaim): no structural obstruction exists yet to WRITING an invalid top-level status; correction/blocking only happens after the fact, if the linter is run or if CI is reached and honored.

MECHANICAL STEPS TAKEN:
1. docs/issues/ISS-0440.yaml: status: instrumented, resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0440-20260903, resolved_at: 2026-09-03T18:12:29Z (UTC, from `date -u`), superseded_by: ISS-0441, plus a resolution_note citing the regression test (test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs) and the design doc (lib/letflow/design/iss440-handoff-status-enforcement.md). related: now also lists ISS-0441, ISS-0442, ISS-0443.
2. GitHub close -- `gh issue close 849 --comment "Investigated in WF03-ISS0440-20260903; verified work shipped but the root cause is NOT removed. See docs/issues/ISS-0440.yaml and the successor issue ISS-0441."` gh output (quoted verbatim): '✓ Closed issue tvolodi/letflow#849 (ISS-0440: Make the handoff top-level status enum violation structurally impossible (7th occurrence; docs/anti-patterns.md declares re-documenting exhausted))'. gh was reachable; no fallback needed.
3. docs/anti-patterns.md -- did NOT add a 7th tally line (the entry already declares that move exhausted after occurrence 6). Instead appended one short paragraph after the 6th-occurrence recurrence note, titled 'ISS-0440 (7th occurrence...): tooling now exists -- go there, not here', pointing at the --autofix remediation path, the HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.3 clause, the design doc, and explicitly naming ISS-0440's own status as `instrumented` (not closed) plus ISS-0441 as the remaining structural gap, with a short 'if this recurs as occurrence 8' runbook (run --autofix first, hand-fix ambiguous values per the tool's refusal message, then read ISS-0441 before writing prose).
4. Confirmed ISS-0442 (status: open, related: [ISS-0440, ISS-0443]) and ISS-0443 (status: open, related: [ISS-0440, ISS-0442]) both correctly cross-reference ISS-0440, and ISS-0440.yaml's own related: now lists both back -- not orphaned.
5. `mix letflow.lint_handoffs` (plain, no --dir/--autofix) run before completing: final line 'letflow.lint_handoffs: OK -- 0 new violations across 1932 handoff files under "handoffs" (25 pre-existing grandfathered, traced to ISS-0190).' Confirmed 0 new violations, run twice (once mid-task, once as the final pre-completion check) with identical result.
